text:
omar: Heads-up — saw a small perf regression on canary yesterday: median token latency +12% on routes that hit a cold KV cache. Trying to prove KV warmup vs kernel choice correlation.

sasha: Which traces? I spotted a cluster around 19:02 UTC with aten_fallback chosen repeatedly (trace ids like abc123...).

liam: I can add a per-request kv_hit_ratio into traces (float) and emit kernel_name + batch_size. That should let us group by low-hit requests.

jess: yes please. Dashboard needs kv_hit_ratio, kernel_name, route_id, and a direct link to the trace. Also add a prefix_cache_warmup boolean so we can isolate first request behaviour.

omar: We should be careful about instrumentation overhead. Suggest sampling at 1% for raw traces and emit aggregated histograms for metrics. e.g. emit a histogram of kv_hit_ratio per route+kernel.

sasha: Plan: compute hits/total at token-commit and emit a histogram metric at request end. Pseudo:```py
# runtime snippet
req.kv_hits += int(is_kv_hit)
req.kv_total += 1
# on finish
metrics.histogram('runtime.kv_hit_ratio', req.kv_hits / max(1, req.kv_total), tags={'kernel': kernel_name, 'route_id': route_id})
```

liam: Two notes: 1) use route_id (not full path) to avoid high cardinality. 2) normalize kernel names (strip build tags) so we don't explode tag space.

jess: For the dashboard UI: waterfall view with kv_hit_ratio buckets on the left (0-20%, 20-50%, 50-80%, 80-100%) and median token latency on the right. Each row should include a "view trace" link that opens tracing UI with the trace_id and pre-filtered span (focus on kv metrics). If kv_hit_ratio < 0.3 show a small warning pill.

omar: Can we also attach minimal per-request metadata into trace context (trace tags) so the UI can construct the link without extra lookups: trace_id, span_id, route_id, kernel_name, kv_hit_ratio (rounded).

deploy-bot: Canary deployment completed: runtime v2.14.3 -> 10% hosts (2026-03-12T19:10:00Z).

sasha: Quick QA: I correlated ~42 low-kv-hit requests to aten_fallback kernel. Pushed a hotfix to prefer quant_kernels when model config supports it — PR #4521. :thumbsup:

liam: I'll run an A/B perf job to compare token latency by kernel with and without KV warmup. Also adding per-route KPI panels for p95 token latency and kv_hit_ratio time-series in Grafana.

jess: Can the trace link open the tracing UI with a pre-populated filter? e.g. "/traces?trace_id=...&filter=kv_hit_ratio%3C0.3" so product folks can click directly.

omar: Great. I'll file tickets: ENG-rt-982 instrument kv_hit_ratio in runtime traces/metrics; ENG-rt-983 dashboard + trace linking; ENG-rt-984 kernel-fallback audit + rollback safety. Will sync with product and infra tomorrow. :calendar:

sasha: Thanks — once metrics emit we'll run a short retrospective to confirm the root cause. If kernel selection is the driver we can add a routing policy to prefer the low-latency kernel for routes with low cache warmup tolerance.

liam: FYI leaving a small note: watch for double-counting when requests are retried or when KV hits are measured across split batches. We'll add a per-request unique id to dedupe.

jess: 👍 keeping this thread as the implementation hub. If anyone adds PRs or dashboards, drop links here.

omar: cheers, tagging followups: @sasha @liam @jess — let's get the instrumentation in this week.
